clue.text: Inlet without outlet in Yorkshire

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the inlet word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
read as 'let out', the letters of LET rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a landlocked inlet with no exit somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking; 'out' in 'outlet' is read as an anagram signal working on LET. BATLEY is a West Yorkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Batley is a mill town in West Yorkshire, so the place lies in that county.

clue.text: Swollen with a plaguey swelling keeping pupil with us

indicators.note: keeping means the swelling holds the pupil inside

parts.note: a bubo is the swollen lymph gland of bubonic plague
L, learner, a pupil
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing something puffed up with a plague sore while minding a student alongside us.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulbous means swollen or rounded, like a bulb.

clue.text: 1 down object of French familiarity and impertinence

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you
lip is cheek, impertinence

explanation.surface: A bulb that inspires French intimacy and cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips grow from bulbs, the theme's 1 down objects.

clue.text: Entire 300 converted, which is weird

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: CCC is 300 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A whole three hundred people changed their faith, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or unconventional, so weird.

clue.text: Old playwright reduced to tell when told

definitions.meaning: A Roman comic dramatist of the second century BC
a name whose short form Tel sounds like the word tell

explanation.surface: An ancient dramatist forced to narrate his story whenever ordered to.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the name: shortened, Terence becomes Tel, which is pronounced like 'tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Terentius Afer, known in English by this name, wrote Latin comedies, making him an old playwright.

clue.text: Novelist has time to stick …

parts.note: T, time
to stick around is to remain

explanation.surface: A writer has the time to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose Tremain is an English novelist. The clue runs on into 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose Tremain is a novelist, author of Restoration.

clue.text: … around one that drank cider

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is '… around one that drank cider': the wordplay needs ROSE (Rose Tremain, the novelist of 4-down) around I, but 'Novelist' is in 4-down's clue, not this one.

clue.text: Hurried up with report of cutter for 1 down object

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: hurried means ran

indicators.note: report of means the word is spoken, giving a rough sound-alike

parts.note: scissors are a cutter

explanation.surface: Rushed up with news of a blade for a bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike is rough: 'scissors' said aloud is close to the end of the flower name.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus plants, including daffodils, grow from bulbs.

clue.text: English drummer's sound produces sea holly

parts.note: E, English

indicators.note: sound means the drummer's name is heard, not written

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer

explanation.surface: An English percussionist's noise yields a coastal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eryngo is Eryngium maritimum, the spiny seaside plant called sea holly.

clue.text: Sailor's evil tautology?

parts.note: saying evil twice: sin and bad, two words for wickedness
bad is the second word for evil, making the repetition

explanation.surface: Asking whether a seaman's wickedness is just saying the same thing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN and BAD both mean evil, so putting them together is a tautology. SINBAD is the sailor of the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Show with little reduced first part for setter

indicators.note: little is cut down to its informal shortening, dropping some letters

parts.note: the opening part of a play is Act One, written ACT I
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Instructions for writing a short opening section of a play on behalf of the puzzle's compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' turns little into LIL, its slangy short form. LILAC TIME is an operetta built on Schubert's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac Time is a stage operetta, and a show is any such theatrical production.

clue.text: Homeless creature's holy light?

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a holy person
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Asking whether an abandoned animal glows with a saintly radiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray is an animal without a home, wandering loose.

clue.text: Artist — did he use golden ink too?

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to ink is to pen, write in ink

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a painter also wrote in gilded ink.
explanation.walkthrough: William Orpen was an Irish portrait painter of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir William Orpen was a painter, a well-known Irish portraitist and war artist.

clue.text: Hail in strait means working hard

indicators.note: the greeting goes inside the name of the strait

parts.note: the Bering Strait separates Alaska and Siberia
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A hailstorm in a channel of sea means the crew must toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is to work industriously, like the busy animal building its dam.

clue.text: Home counties successfully treated and guaranteed

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
a patient successfully treated is cured

explanation.surface: Patients in the region near London were healed and their recovery assured.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties bordering London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Secured and guaranteed both mean made certain or safe, as a loan backed by collateral.

clue.text: Origin of 17 or insect or bird

parts.note: a crocus grows from a corm
taken as written
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Musing whether something began as a flower, a bug or a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a large dark diving seabird.

clue.text: Crazy fellow embracing underworld without cover?

indicators.note: embracing means the madman's word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the realm itself

explanation.surface: A madman hugging the land of the dead without any protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, so has no covering at all.

clue.text: 1 down objects to remove when rising in assemblies

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the assemblies

parts.note: the Dáil is the Irish parliament, plural Dails

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to doff is to remove, as a hat

explanation.surface: Bulbs to be taken out when meetings stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rising' reads 'to remove' upwards, as this is a down clue; the Dáil is Ireland's parliament, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils grow from bulbs, the theme's 1 down objects.

clue.text: Reptile, American, not technically 1 down object

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile
US, United States, American

explanation.surface: A crocodile from America that is not strictly a bulbous creature.
explanation.walkthrough: This flower grows from a corm, not a true bulb, hence 'not technically'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus springs from a corm, which gardeners often loosely call a bulb, though botanically it differs.

clue.text: 1 down object put everyone in picture — with lady, say?

indicators.note: everyone goes inside the picture

parts.note: a shot is a photograph, a picture
all, everyone

explanation.surface: A bulb that puts the whole crowd in a photograph, along with a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with lady, say?' hints at Tennyson's The Lady of Shalott, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The shallot is a small onion-like plant grown from a bulb.

clue.text: No failures possible if I depart

indicators.note: possible signals the letters can be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written: the letter to depart from the pool

explanation.surface: An optimistic claim that nothing could go wrong once I leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle FAILURES after taking out the I ('if I depart').
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no, the answer given when declining.

clue.text: Enjoyment of quarrel is horrible

indicators.note: of signals the answer comes out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Relishing a quarrel is a dreadful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish is keen enjoyment or zest.

clue.text: Pole that's put in fast — that's not too hard

indicators.note: put in means the pieces are placed inside the fast

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
N, north pole
i.e., id est, that is

explanation.surface: A post driven quickly into the ground that is not too difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means merciful, not severe, so not too hard on someone.

clue.text: 1 down object, French, with one change of side

indicators.note: one left becomes right: one L swapped for R

parts.note: Gallic means French

explanation.surface: A French bulb that switched sides once.
explanation.walkthrough: One L (left) in GALLIC changes to R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic grows as a bulb made of cloves.

clue.text: It will take ages going by the side of the mansion as stated

indicators.note: as stated means the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.words: going by the side of the mansion
parts.note: passing alongside the stately home: along hall

explanation.surface: A slow walk past a grand house that takes forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A long haul is a lengthy, arduous task or journey, one that takes ages.

clue.text: Sharp blow round 19

parts.note: a gust is a sharp blow of wind
O is round

explanation.surface: A sudden blast of wind around clue 19.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, the same as relish.

clue.text: 1 down object of 12 twisted round the next

indicators.note: the scrambled midday word goes round the next hour
twisted means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: twelve o'clock is noon
the hour after twelve is one, the numeral I

explanation.surface: A bulb from clue 12, contorted round whatever follows.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' here is the time: NOON, scrambled to ONON, goes round I, the hour that comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: The onion grows from a true bulb, the theme's subject.

clue.text: Employed from -8?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Employed from -8?': the answer is hidden in '-8' spelt out as 'minus eight'; the printed figures hold no letters, so the hidden-word check cannot find it and the whole-clue form is refused as a downgrade.

clue.text: 1 down objects heard in betrayal of secrets

indicators.note: heard means the word for the vegetables is spoken

parts.note: leeks are bulbous vegetables of the onion family

explanation.surface: Bulbs overheard in an act of treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaks are disclosures of confidential information, betrayal of secrets.

clue.text: Weariness — it's not quite due to being led by a girl

indicators.note: being led by puts the girl first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: a lass is a girl
it, with the 's as a link

indicators.note: not quite, not right, signals that due is scrambled

explanation.surface: Tiredness that is almost owed to a young woman leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental weariness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Sailing vessel attaching pet snake to bottom of mast

parts.note: a cat is a pet
a boa is a snake

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Tying a pet snake to the foot of a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A catboat is a small sailboat with one mast stepped far forward.

clue.text: Massive space for badgers in Yorkshire

parts.note: OS, outsize, massive
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: A huge badger burrow somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: OSSETT is a West Yorkshire town near Batley.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossett is a town in West Yorkshire, so it lies in that county.
